      - term: United Kingdom
      - definition:
        - text: In the UK, a GHK-Cu serum sold for appearance is a cosmetic, and cosmetics law excludes anything injected (September 2026).
        - generic: "Source: Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 on cosmetic products (assimilated law, as it applies in Great Britain), Article 2 — Definitions · A guide to what is a medicinal product — MHRA Guidance Note 8"
      - term: European Union
      - definition:
        - text: In the EU, copper tripeptide-1 is listed in the Commission's CosIng inventory with a skin-conditioning function (read 25 September 2026). No centrally authorised medicine containing GHK-Cu was found in the Union Register or in EMA's data on authorised, refused and withdrawn medicines (searched 25 September 2026).
        - generic: "Source: CosIng ingredient record: COPPER TRIPEPTIDE-1 · CosIng — Cosmetic ingredients database (notice on legal status) · Download medicine data — EMA medicines data table (centrally authorised, refused, withdrawn and withdrawn-application medicines) · Union Register of medicinal products for human use (authorised, not active and refused lists)"
      - term: Portugal
      - definition:
        - text: In Portugal, no medicine containing GHK-Cu is listed in INFARMED's Infomed register, which includes authorised, lapsed and revoked products (searched 25 September 2026).
        - generic: "Source: Infomed – base de dados de medicamentos do Infarmed (pesquisa avançada and 'Detalhes do Medicamento' pages)"
      - term: Brazil
      - definition:
        - text: In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that products presented as peptides called GHK-Cu that promise aesthetic effects or improvement in health conditions are not registered with Anvisa.
        - generic: "Source: Checamos: peptídeos que prometem milagres NÃO estão registrados na Anvisa"
      - term: United Arab Emirates
      - definition:
        - text: In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has held medicines registration since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023, and no registered medical product matching GHK, prezatide, copper tripeptide or copper peptide was found in the EDE register (25 September 2026). In Dubai, the DHA's rules for health facilities prohibit circulating, prescribing, dispensing, administering or using any peptide product unless it is registered or licensed with the EDE (29 July 2026); in Abu Dhabi, the DoH classes topical cosmetic peptides with no systemic effect as low-risk products that stay under existing regulatory pathways, while systemic, regenerative or weakly evidenced peptides face enhanced controls (31 July 2026).
        - generic: "Source: Federal Decree-Law No. (28) of 2023 On the Establishment of the UAE Drug Corporation (official English translation) · Registered medical product directory (Drug Directory) · DHA External Circular DHA/OUT/2026/0000867: Regulations for Handling Peptide Products in Healthcare Facilities (technical annex) · DoH Circular No. (148)/2026: Mandatory Requirements for Peptide Products"
      - term: Saudi Arabia
      - definition: "Saudi context: distinguish a topical GHK-Cu cosmetic from an injectable product. This review has not verified the local status of an exact product in either category. An FDA classification does not establish Saudi permission. Check product category, route, claims and the SFDA record."
    - paragraph: Every peptide question has four separate answers. For GHK-Cu they point in different directions, which is exactly why they must not be blended into one sentence.
    - strong: Mechanism
    - generic: Plausible
    - generic: Copper delivery to matrix and antioxidant enzymes; gene-expression data from the originator
    - strong: Human evidence
    - generic: "Topical: GRADE C · Injectable: none"
    - generic: One small indexed RCT and sponsor-run cosmetic trials; no randomized trials of injection
    - strong: Regulatory status (US, 14 May 2026)
    - generic: "Non-injectable: 503A Category 1"
    - generic: Category 1 means FDA is still evaluating and does not intend to act against compounders who meet its conditions; an advisory-committee consultation is planned before the end of February 2027. The injectable route has no such standing.
    - strong: Open question
    - generic: Does it reach the dermis?
    - generic: Penetration data are in vitro and depend on how they are measured
    - paragraph: A strong mechanism is not a strong trial, and a Category 1 listing is not an approval.
